facts.text: README.md states that the repository is ported to Gazebo Harmonic and ROS 2 Jazzy.
competition_bridges always includes the clock and task_info bridges in its bridge list.
competition_bridges constructs one ros_gz_bridge parameter_bridge Node with the arguments and remappings of its bridge list.
bridges.clock maps Gazebo /clock to ROS /clock as rosgraph_msgs/msg/Clock with the GZ_TO_ROS direction.
bridges.task_info maps Gazebo /vrx/task/info to ROS /vrx/task/info as ros_gz_interfaces/msg/ParamVec with the GZ_TO_ROS direction.
ScoringPlugin defaults its task-info topic to /vrx/task/info.
ScoringPlugin advertises a Gazebo msgs::Param publisher on the task-info topic.
ScoringPlugin::UpdateTaskMessage sets state, elapsed_time, remaining_time, timed_out, num_collisions and score, and PublishStats publishes them at 1 Hz.
Model.is_UAV recognizes vrx_hexrotor and vrx_quadrotor, while Model.is_USV recognizes usv and wam-v.
Model.is_UAV returns whether the model type is in UAVS and is_USV whether it is in USVS.
Model.bridges appends cmd_vel only inside the is_UAV branch; the is_USV branch performs no command bridge.
launch.spawn places the bridge and helper nodes in a PushRosNamespace(model.model_name) group.
competition.launch.py defaults the spawned robot name to wamv and its model type to wam-v.
launch.simulation starts ros_gz_sim's gz_sim launch and passes -r unless the launch was given paused; the paused flag is a launch argument, not a ROS service.
Model.payload_from_sdf records each gz::sim::systems::Thruster and JointPositionController plugin as a thruster_thrust_<name> or thruster_rotate_<name> payload entry.
payload_bridges dispatches thruster_thrust_* entries to thrust() and thruster_rotate_* entries to thrust_joint_pos().
payload_bridges.thrust maps ROS thrusters/<side>/thrust to Gazebo <model>/thrusters/<side>/thrust as std_msgs/msg/Float64 with the ROS_TO_GZ direction.
payload_bridges.thrust_joint_pos maps ROS thrusters/<side>/pos to Gazebo <model>/thrusters/<side>/pos as std_msgs/msg/Float64 with the ROS_TO_GZ direction.
The shipped wamv.yaml teleop configuration names /wamv/thrusters/left/thrust with std_msgs/msg/Float64.
The shipped wamv.yaml teleop configuration names /wamv/thrusters/right/thrust with std_msgs/msg/Float64.
The shipped wamv.yaml teleop configuration names /wamv/thrusters/left/pos with std_msgs/msg/Float64.
The shipped wamv.yaml teleop configuration names /wamv/thrusters/right/pos with std_msgs/msg/Float64.
The WAM-V thruster macro configures gz-sim-thruster-system on topic thrusters/<name>/thrust with velocity_control true.
The WAM-V thruster macro configures gz-sim-joint-position-controller-system on topic <namespace>/thrusters/<name>/pos.
competition.launch.py declares the world argument with the default sydney_regatta.
sydney_regatta.sdf names its world sydney_regatta.
navigation_task.sdf also names its world sydney_regatta.
The sydney_regatta GUI configuration loads the WorldControl plugin with play/pause and step enabled.
ScoringPlugin's PreUpdate updates the time from the simulation time, updates the task state and calls PublishStats.
ScoringPlugin's PublishStats publishes the task message once per second of the plugin's current time.
The README names a humble branch for users who continue with Gazebo Garden and ROS 2 Humble.
SimulationRunner composes its transport namespace as /world/ followed by the world name.
SimulationRunner advertises the control service with OnWorldControl as its callback.
OnWorldControl copies the WorldControl request into a WorldControlState and calls OnWorldControlState.
OnWorldControlState appends the control to worldControls and sets the Boolean reply to true.
ProcessWorldControl calls SetPaused with the pause flag of each queued control.
A queued control with multi_step on a paused world adds the steps and unpauses the world so that stepping can occur.
SetPaused stores the pause state in currentInfo.paused.
Step publishes the world statistics.
Step processes the world control messages.
The Run loop calls Step on every iteration and counts a processed iteration only while not paused.
The statistics publisher on the stats topic is limited to 10 messages per second.
PublishStats copies currentInfo.paused into the WorldStatistics message.
UpdateCurrentInfo advances the simulation time and the iteration count only while not paused.
The Physics system steps the physics only when not paused.
The Thruster system's thrust callback stores the clamped thrust command.
The Thruster system's PreUpdate returns early while paused.
The joint position controller's position callback stores the commanded position.
The joint position controller's PreUpdate returns early while paused.
The bridge maps ros_gz_interfaces/srv/ControlWorld to a gz.msgs.WorldControl request with a gz.msgs.Boolean reply.
The ControlWorld response's success is the gz Boolean reply's data.
For a failed gz request the ControlWorld response's success is false.
The service bridge converts each ROS request and sends it with gz Request and a callback that sends the ROS response.
Node::Request with a callback requests a service using a non-blocking call.
The WorldStatistics conversion copies the gz header into the ROS header and copies paused.
ros_gz_interfaces WorldStatistics carries a header, sim_time, pause_time, real_time and the paused flag.
ControlWorld takes a WorldControl request and answers bool success.
WorldControl's fields include pause, step and multi_step.
ros_gz_interfaces ParamVec carries a header and rcl_interfaces Parameter entries.
The bridge README maps ros_gz_interfaces/msg/WorldStatistics to gz.msgs.WorldStatistics.
The bridge README maps the ros_gz_interfaces/srv/ControlWorld service to gz.msgs.WorldControl and gz.msgs.Boolean.
The bridge README's service example starts parameter_bridge with a /world/<name>/control ControlWorld argument.
Without a configured QoS profile the bridge's publisher QoS is KeepLast with the publisher queue size.
The bridge's publisher allows its deadline, depth, durability, history, liveliness and reliability QoS to be overridden.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned replies with no physics step or state-hash replay; its world statistics follow the wall clock

gaps: the fake is a ROS-free canned transport: it answers the /clock and /vrx/task/info subscriptions and records the four /wamv thruster publications, but runs no Gazebo physics, thruster system, buoyancy, waves, wind, contacts, sensors or ROS graph
clock samples and task-info entries are placeholders; a live run must receive /clock and /vrx/task/info from the operator's ros_gz_bridge and scoring plugin

the task-info topic is published by a scoring plugin once per second of simulation time (ScoringPlugin.cc:327-337); worlds without that plugin or a competition bridge, and a paused world, publish no fresh task sample and the explicit observation must time out

the /wamv thruster topics exist only when the shipped launch detects the Thruster and JointPositionController plugins and pushes the model name as the ROS namespace; the package assumes the default name wamv, and a renamed model requires matching endpoint configuration
a thruster publication is transmission-only; the fake does not model the gz thruster system's max_thrust_cmd clamp or any resulting motion; each receipt reports the value it handed to rosbridge

the stop is the companion gz-sim world pause (WorldControl through ros_gz ControlWorld), whose reply is true for any request gz-sim queued (SimulationRunner.cc:1375-1377); it is confirmed by the E2 read-back: the fake keeps a paused flag that the control request sets after its next statistics sample and publishes /world/sydney_regatta/stats every 100 ms (placeholder) while subscribed; it runs no SimulationRunner

the e-stop endpoints exist only while the operator runs ros_gz's parameter_bridge with the two arguments of operator_bridges (competition_bridges and spawn bridge topics only, launch.py:255-259, 311-318, 346-363); without them the control call is not answered and the read-back sees no sample, so the e-stop fails closed; the declared estop_latency_ms 1500 covers the control call (400 ms) and the read-back bound (600 ms)

the read-back's freshness is the arrival time only: the bridged WorldStatistics header is the gz header, which PublishStats does not stamp (ros_gz convert copies it, ros_gz_interfaces.cpp:840); the bridge's default publisher QoS sets only KeepLast with the queue size (bridge_config.cpp:274-279), so its durability stays rclcpp's default, volatile, which replays no history to a late subscriber; the first sample is discarded and a burst of samples restarts the count; an operator QoS override of the stats publisher (factory.hpp:61-82) to a deeper transient-local history is not covered beyond that burst rule

the endpoints name the default world sydney_regatta (competition.launch.py:68-71, sydney_regatta.sdf:4; navigation_task.sdf reuses the name); the other task worlds carry their own names, and with them the declared endpoints do not exist and the e-stop fails closed

a live world can be unpaused or stepped by the Gazebo GUI's world control (play, pause and step, sydney_regatta.sdf:115-134), a WorldControl multi_step (SimulationRunner.cc:1445-1452) or any client of the control service; MHS does not watch the flag after the e-stop (safety_status re-reads it only on request)

no unpause is offered: the Thruster system stores the last thrust command (Thruster.cc:517-526) and the joint position controller the last angle target (JointPositionController.cc:489-492), and buoyancy, waves and wind act on the hull as soon as the world steps; a zero thrust on both sides would replace the stored thrust only unacknowledged, and the angle target cannot be cleared without a joint reading this package does not have; after mhs.safety.reset the world stays paused, commands are stored for the next unpause, and the operator publishes zero thrust (and the wanted angles), checks the GUI and other publishers (the joystick teleop, wamv.yaml:75-119), then unpauses outside MHS (the GUI play button or a ControlWorld request with pause false)

the deployment's gz-sim, ros_gz and gz-transport must be the pinned 8.15.0, 1.0.25 and 13.6.0 releases (ROS 2 Jazzy with Gazebo Harmonic); the README names a humble branch for Gazebo Garden and ROS 2 Humble (README.md:18), which this package does not serve; rosbridge cannot read the versions

safe_state.description: The world sydney_regatta is paused: after the WorldControl pause two fresh stats samples, 40 ms or more apart within 600 ms, reported paused true, so the world does not step and the thrusters apply no thrust; it is the paused flag in that window, not a measured standstill, it needs the operator-run ros_gz bridges, and no unpause is offered: stored thrust and angle targets, waves and wind act when the operator resumes it.
